ch14.note: 'Returned students' (留学生, liuxuesheng) were Chinese who had studied abroad—most often in Japan, but also in Europe and America—and come home. In Republican China they formed a prized, Western- or Japanese-trained elite, and the label carried real prestige.

Chinese military ranks fell in three tiers: general-grade (将), field-grade (校: colonel, lieutenant colonel, major), and company-grade (尉: the junior captains and lieutenants). 'Field-grade' thus names the middle, senior-but-not-general officers.
